 Residents urged to apply for utility bill aid by Board of Public Utilities for benefits up to $200 a month
 By ROI-NJ Staff 
 November 2, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Linkedin 
 NJBPU President Ben Hertz-Shargel. - courtesy NJ.gov
 The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) is encouraging eligible households to take advantage of utility bill aid through the state’s Universal Service Fund (USF), as the new energy aid application period officially opened Oct. 1.
 Administered by the New Jersey Department of Community Affairs (NJDCA), USF helps eligible low-to-moderate households keep their monthly electric and natural gas bills at an affordable amount.
 “Affordability is at the center of everything we’re doing at the Board, and that means making sure New Jersey families can access the aid they need to manage their utility bills,” NJBPU President Ben Hertz-Shargel said.
 “These expanded benefits put more money back into household budgets, and our work with utilities and community partners will help connect more eligible residents with aid. We want every New Jerseyan who qualifies for these programs to know that help is available and that applying is easier than they may think.”
 The USF program now provides minimum monthly bill credits of $20 for gas and electric each, quadruple the previous $5 minimum, and provides maximum bill credits of $200 per month, up from $180, for gas and electric combined. The board approved these increases to USF benefits last year and these enhancements continue to provide meaningful financial relief for households struggling with energy costs.
 Additionally, the Board ordered the seven gas and electric utility companies to assist first-time enrollees with their applications, which has increased program access statewide.
 Enrolling in USF also provides households with access to other programs, such as the federal Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (“LIHEAP”) and the USF-Fresh Start energy debt forgiveness program. Participating in USF also provides protections from utility shut off during the winter and summer months.
 Starting Oct. 1, New Jersey households can apply with one application for both the USF and federal LIHEAP benefits at: www.nj.gov/dca/dcaid . Customers can receive benefits from both programs at the same time.
 While USF delivers recurring monthly credits that help eligible households better afford natural gas and electric service, LIHEAP provides lump sum benefit aid with home heating costs, including gas, electric, deliverable fuels and help for those with energy costs included in rent. LIHEAP also provides medically necessary cooling expenses, emergency aid funds when in danger of disconnection and heating repair and replacement.
 Income limits and program eligibility information is available at: www.energyassistance.nj.gov . Residents can also call 1-800-510-3102 for information about program eligibility, available aid, where they can seek in person help locally and application status updates.
 The LIHEAP application period runs from Oct. 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis while funding remains available. Eligible residents are encouraged to apply promptly.
